headline.text: Across overlapping categories, county crude shares lag nationally for life-prolonging treatment (20.3%, 95% CI 17.3–23.8 vs 30.4%) and recorded MDT meetings (0.2%, 95% CI 0.0–0.9 vs 6.0%).

details.text: The county's crude life-prolonging treatment share is 20.3% (95% CI 17.3–23.8; n=121/595) compared with 30.4% (4522/14873) nationally, and its 95% confidence interval excludes the national value.

An MDT meeting is recorded for a crude share of 0.2% of county patients (95% CI 0.0–0.9; n=1/595) versus 6.0% (893/14873) nationally, with the 95% confidence interval excluding the national value, though HILMO MDT codes measure recording practice from direct patient contacts rather than care.

Because treatment categories overlap and a patient can have several treatments, the county's crude curative share of 35.6% (95% CI 31.9–39.6; n=212/595) has a 95% confidence interval above the national 27.0% (4009/14873), whereas the crude symptomatic share of 36.1% (95% CI 32.4–40.1; n=215/595) includes the national 39.5% (5871/14873) in its 95% confidence interval.

The crude share of patients with no treatment record within 12 months is 28.9% (95% CI 25.4–32.7; n=172/595) compared with 27.5% (4089/14873) nationally, a category whose 95% confidence interval includes the national value and that mixes untreated patients with unrecorded treatment.

headline.text: County treatment shares in Taulukko 11 are crude—neither age-adjusted nor stage-adjusted—and public registry data do not capture pathway waiting times before or after diagnosis.

details.text: Taulukko 11 gives crude county shares with separate limitations: they are not age-adjusted (county age-adjusted shares appear only in the Kuva 16 figure, where digitised national curative reference lines at ±0.5 percentage points are 26.7% for men and 26.9% for women), and independently, they cannot be stage-adjusted because stage at diagnosis is missing for about 48% of patients.

A journal article found that HILMO diagnoses match the Cancer Registry for about 90% of most cancer types, which supports diagnosis concordance only and says nothing about treatment, referral or MDT recording, while Finland has no cancer quality registry and lung cancer data collection remains incomplete.

In the report, symptoms and referrals are not measured, primary care visits are not included in the report's data, occupational health is not mentioned, imaging appears only indirectly as the diagnosis basis for about 20% of patients, and HILMO records whether a specialist visit (93.6%) or treatment occurred within 12 months but not when it started.

Preliminary, unpublished figures from an MOT study show lung cancer in Finland takes 155 days on average from symptoms to treatment versus 107 days in Sweden and 67 days in Denmark—comprising 56 days of patient delay, 41 days in primary care and 58 days in specialist care—but these preliminary figures are national averages, not county data.

headline.text: The team recommends publishing how completely stage, drug treatment and MDT meetings are recorded, tracking access times with THL 21/2016 definitions, and standardising referrals and diagnostic-phase coordination.

details.text: Given the county's overlapping crude shares for recorded MDT meetings at 0.2% (95% CI 0.0–0.9; n=1/595) versus 6.0% nationally and life-prolonging treatment at 20.3% (95% CI 17.3–23.8; n=121/595) versus 30.4% nationally—alongside missing stage for about 48% of patients and incomplete data collection—the team recommends publishing per county how completely stage, drug treatment and MDT meetings are recorded.

Because the Health Care Act §52 sets no maximum time for a cancer suspicion and Finland lacks national pathway monitoring, the team recommends reporting access times using THL Ohjaus 21/2016 definitions for 16 cancers and flagging stalled handovers while the Filha programme's diagnostics recommendation with specialist-care time limits is to be carried out before the 2030 mid-term evaluation.

The team recommends adopting a referral template and persistent-symptoms rule modelled on KYS's regional pathway document and naming a diagnostic-phase contact person, as local referral practices vary, mentor insight notes weak referrals get lower urgency ratings, and the STM roadmap's measure 1.2.3 plans care-coordinator guidance by 2026–2028 for county adoption by 2029–2031 without specifying the care phase.

q:4e702a20fe.claim_text: Finland has no unified national system to steer the drafting of cancer-specific treatment recommendations, or the implementation and monitoring of care pathways based on them (quality and effectiveness targets/indicators, including access to care, and cancer-specific and generic PROMs). Existing recommendations and pathways, and the targets and indicators to be monitored, are not coordinated nationally. This maintains regional inequality in the availability and effectiveness of cancer care.
q:4e702a20fe.quote: Suomessa ei ole yhtenäistä kansallista järjestelmää, joka ohjaisi syöpäkohtaisten hoitosuositusten laatimista sekä niihin perustuvien hoitoketjujen toteutusta ja seurantaa (laatu- ja vaikuttavuustavoitteet/indikaattorit, mukaan lukien hoitoonpääsy sekä syöpäkohtaiset ja geneeriset PROM-vointimittarit). Olemassa olevia hoitosuosituksia ja -ketjuja sekä seurattavia tavoitteita ja indikaattoreita ei koordinoida kansallisella tasolla. Tämä ylläpitää alueellista eriarvoisuutta syövän hoidon saatavuudessa ja vaikuttavuudessa.
q:4e702a20fe.quote_en: Finland does not have a uniform national system to guide the preparation of cancer-specific clinical guidelines and the implementation and monitoring of care pathways based on them (quality and effectiveness targets/indicators, including access to care as well as cancer-specific and generic PROM well-being measures). Existing clinical guidelines and care pathways as well as monitored targets and indicators are not coordinated at the national level. This maintains regional inequality in the availability and effectiveness of cancer care.

Until national target times exist, flag stalled handovers.
